Claude's conclusion:
**Root cause:** This is a timing race between the test's 300‑second wait window and nim's default periodic DPC/connectivity retest cadence, not an EVE network bug. Live `nim` logs show the DPC (`zedagent`) first reached `DPC_SUCCESS` at `23:24:18.901`, then went completely idle until a scheduled periodic re-test fired at `23:28:52` (`Calling dhcpcd -U -4/-6 eth0`) and finally logged `TestConnectivity: connectivity test SUCCEEDED for URL: adam.evetest:443` / published the new `LastSucceeded` at `23:29:20.551` — 301.65s after the prior success, i.e. just ~2 seconds past the test's 300s deadline. The device's config has no override for `timer.port.testinterval`, so it uses pillar's compiled-in default of 300s (`pkg/pillar/types/globalconfigold.go:99` / `types/global.go:1226`), which lines up almost exactly with the test's own 300s timeout — nim's retest was simply scheduled to land at t+300s and happened to finish a hair after the test gave up, rather than any connectivity actually being broken (IPv6 connectivity itself was fine throughout: `eth0` kept its IPv6 address and DNS server the whole time).

The broker (`farfalle`) is running fairly hot (86% of host RAM assigned to running VMs, load ~6/40, 1.9 GiB swap in use) but CPU itself is idle (3%), so this doesn't look like gross host overload — the 5‑minute retest cadence by itself is enough to explain the ~2s overshoot even on a healthy host. I found no other failure in this run to compare a shared root cause against, and I didn't find this test (`TestDeviceIPv6Connectivity`) or the `"DPC LastSucceeded has advanced"` signature anywhere in `live-ledger.md`, so this is a new/first-seen failure signature, not a previously documented recurring issue — though it looks like an inherent race against nim's 300s default retest interval that could plausibly recur whenever the first periodic retest lands even a couple seconds late (e.g. under any added scheduling jitter from host load).

Claude's conclusion:
Host is healthy (7% CPU, load 1.07, no meaningful swap), ruling out infra contention.

**Root cause:** This is the same long-known, recurring `TestVMAppPurgeDuringFailover` designated-node deadlock documented extensively in the ledger (first seen 2026-10-29, introduced by commit `98acf1411`, reproducing in the large majority of nightly runs since). Live evidence matches exactly: `edge-dev1` (the app's designated node) is `EVE_DEVICE_STATE_SUSPECT` (deliberately taken offline by the test to simulate failover), and `kubectl get vmirs,vmi,vm,pod -A` from `edge-dev2` returns zero VMIRS/VMI/VM anywhere in the cluster — only infra pods (cdi, kubevirt, longhorn-system, kube-system) — exactly matching the test's `found []`. `edge-dev2`'s live `/run/zedkube/ENClusterAppStatus/` for app `failover-purge-app` (uuid `3de48314-...`) shows `IsDNidNode:false, ScheduledOnThisNode:false, AppKubeStatus:NotInCluster`, and `zedkube`'s log is still looping unbroken through the current moment, repeating `newStatus:{...false false Unknown false 0}` every ~10s — no surviving node is the designated node, so none ever re-requests a VMIRS after the purge tore down the old one. The broker host is healthy (7% CPU, load 1.07, negligible swap), ruling out resource contention. This doesn't share a root cause with any other failure investigated in this run; it's simply the latest instance of the same month-old, unresolved deadlock.

--- TestClusterPVCRedownload ---
Device "edge-dev3": expected 1 reboot(s) but observed 2

Claude's conclusion:
No prior occurrences in the ledger — this looks like a new failure signature.

### Root cause

Live evidence on `edge-dev3` shows this is a real self-healing reboot, not a crash: from `00:29:13` through `00:34:22` its local pillar/zedkube process repeatedly failed TLS verification against the node's own k3s API server (`127.0.0.1:6443`) with `tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` against `k3s-server-ca@1795825455`, while the init log shows a clean, cooperative `/bin/rc.shutdown` sequence at `00:34:53` followed by a fresh kernel boot at `00:35:21` — no kernel panic, OOM, or watchdog-hard-reset anywhere in the logs. This exactly matches `pkg/kube/kube-init/monitor/transition.go`'s cluster-join-stall watchdog (`joinStallTimeout = 5 * time.Minute`), which reboots a node that makes no forward progress joining the cluster for 5 minutes — a legitimate, intentional recovery path, not a bug in EVE's reboot behavior itself. The actual bug is on the evetest harness side: `evetest/edgedevice.go`'s `ApplyConfig` only calls `ExpectAdditionalReboots`/`incExpectedRebootCount` for the "leaving cluster mode" reboot case, with no equivalent accounting for this join-stall retry reboot during initial cluster formation, so when it legitimately fires the harness's `checkRebootCounts` audit miscounts and flags `edge-dev3: expected 1 reboot(s) but observed 2`.

timed out after 5m0.000767114s (excluding download) waiting for app "ac3840d3-d24b-4f12-b080-774fd32ae3d0" (app-1) on device "edge-dev" to reach RUNNING state (last state: RESOLVING_TAG)

Claude's conclusion:
### Root cause

Live evidence confirms this is the same known "hung image tag-resolve" family already documented in the ledger, but with a new detail that pins down the actual mechanism. `app-1`'s content tree (`0ff24197-...`, image `lfedge/evetest-ubuntu-ctr:1.2`) and `app-2`'s sibling request both started their `handleResolveCreate` calls concurrently at 23:27:30. `app-2` resolved normally ~3 minutes later (23:30:26, `State:108`), but `app-1`'s resolve made no further progress for the full 5-minute test window (`/run/downloader/ResolveStatus/` was empty the whole time — no persisted resolve status, matching the "vanished" signature from past occurrences). Checking back live, `app-1` did eventually recover: `evetest eve app-info` shows an explicit app error fired at 23:37:30 — `"no response from the transport for lfedge/evetest-ubuntu-ctr:1.2 in 10m0.000431206s, cancelling"` — after which the retry succeeded immediately and the app progressed through INSTALLED → BOOTING → RUNNING by 23:38:37. So the resolve wasn't actually hung forever, it was blocked on a 10-minute internal transport timeout (go-containerregistry `remote.Get` call) that is more than double the test's 5-minute wait, guaranteeing a timeout regardless.

This is a known, recurring issue per `live-ledger.md`: the identical "one of two concurrent tag-resolve requests stalls while the sibling resolves quickly" signature for this exact test (`TestSwitchNIDeletedWithAppsAttached`) was first seen 2026-11-02, and the same downloader/resolve-hang mechanism has recurred repeatedly since (including `TestFlowLog`/`acl-app` variants). Tonight's occurrence adds new evidence not previously captured — the actual 10-minute transport-timeout/cancel/retry cycle — pinpointing that the root bug is an excessively long internal transport timeout in the OCI registry resolve path rather than a true infinite hang. The broker host is fairly loaded (99% of host memory committed to running VMs, load ~4-6 on 32 CPUs) but not obviously overloaded, so this looks like the long-standing code-level issue rather than a new infra-contention cause. No PR diff was supplied, so no relatedness verdict applies.

Device "edge-dev2": expected 1 reboot(s) but observed 2

Claude's conclusion:
Host is 97% committed to VM memory with 20/20 VMs running — consistent with the resource contention that's long been correlated with this exact failure family.

### Root cause

Live `NodeAgentStatus` on `edge-dev2` confirms `RebootReason: "[2026-11-28 02:49:34]: BootReasonKubeTransition, Reboot after retry cluster transition attempt 1"`, and the harness log shows this reboot (restart counter 0→1, "total observed reboots this test: 1") happening at 02:50:40 — **before** the test's own deliberate power-off/power-on cycle for `edge-dev2` at 02:53:57/02:55:56 (which itself correctly incremented the counter to 2). So the extra, unaccounted-for reboot is EVE-K's own retry logic self-rebooting `edge-dev2` after its cluster-join stalled, landing an extra reboot on top of the one the test expects, which is exactly what tripped `checkRebootCounts`' "expected 1 reboot(s) but observed 2."

This is the identical `BootReasonKubeTransition`/"stuck cluster-join → EVE-K retry self-reboot" mechanism already documented in `live-ledger.md`, known and recurring since at least 2026-10-29, with the two most recent prior instances on 2026-11-23 (run #41, both on `edge-dev2`, in `TestThreeNodesCluster` and `TestMgmtProxy`). Tonight's occurrence is a third manifestation of the same bug, now hitting `TestTwoNodeHACluster`. The broker is at 97% host-RAM commitment with all 20 VMs running and some swap in use, matching the resource-contention pattern that's repeatedly correlated with slow cluster convergence triggering this retry-reboot path, though as before I can't prove causation beyond that correlation. This doesn't share a root cause with any other failure in this run (no other failures reported yet this run per the ledger/artifacts).
